description: Task 2 — wires the block-swap symmetrization shift ΔB=scale·log(S_free/S_atom) (task 1) into the ⁴He log-ratio binding and tests closure. RESULT: the shift is O(0.3–1.5 MeV), a few %% of the O(20–26 MeV) AME gap, and sign-only points the wrong way — so the identical-nucleon symmetrization is a real but SUB-DOMINANT correction; the binding form/convention is the dominant gate, not the symmetrization. Sign-only convention (self-consistent); averaged is the slow refinement, verdict convention-robust.

data.verdict: Symmetrization does NOT close the ⁴He gate: the shift scale·log(S_free/S_atom) is O(0.3–1.5 MeV) — only a few %% of the O(20–26 MeV) gap to AME — and (sign-only) it points the WRONG way (S_free<S_atom ⇒ negative shift, deepening the under-prediction). The binding-form / trace-convention is the dominant gap, NOT the identical-particle symmetrization. The symmetrization is a real but sub-dominant O(1 MeV) correction; the averaged-convention sign/magnitude is the slow-path refinement, but the order-of-magnitude verdict (shift ≪ gap) is convention-robust.
